pages.text: FUNCTIONS AND RELATIONS

RELATIONS
A relation is any set of ordered pairs. The set of all the x-components of the ordered pairs is called the domain of the relation and the set of all the y-components is called the range.  It is a subset of the Cartesian product.

Example:
{(-2, 1), (4, 3), (7, -3)}, usually written in set notation form with curly brackets.

TYPES OF RELATIONS
Empty Relations
Universal Relations
Identity Relations
Inverse Relations
Reflexive Relations
Symmetric Relations
Transitive Relations

TYPES OF RELATIONS — DEFINITIONS

Empty Relation: no element is related to any element.
Universal Relation: every element is related to every element.
Identity Relation: every element is related to itself.
Inverse Relation: reverses each ordered pair.
Reflexive: every element is related to itself.
Symmetric: if (a,b) is included, (b,a) is included.
Transitive: if (a,b) and (b,c) are included, (a,c) is included.

DOMAIN AND RANGE
DOMAIN – It is a collection of the first values in the ordered pair (Set of all input (x) values).
RANGE – It is a collection of the second values in the ordered pair (Set of all output (y) values).

FUNCTIONS
A relation in which each member of the domain is paired exactly one member of the range (a set of ordered pairs) is called a function..
One input = only one output.

TYPE OF FUNCTIONS
One to one function or Injective function
A function f: P → Q is said to be one to one if for each element of P there is a distinct element of Q
Many to one function
A function which maps two or more elements of P to the same element of set Q.

TYPE OF FUNCTIONS
Onto Function or Surjective function
A function for which every element of set Q there is pre-image in set P.
One to one correspondence or Bijective function
The function f matches with each element of P with a discrete element of Q and every element of Q has pre-image in P.

Functions as a graph in the Cartesian Plane.
Given the graph of a relation, we can easily identify if it is a function or not by using the Vertical Line Test.
A graph of a mathematical relation is said to be a function if any vertical line drawn passing through the graph touches the graph at exactly one point.
QUIZ 2

5. If a vertical line intersects a graph in more than one point, the graph:

A) Represents a function
B) Does not represent a function
C) Represents a one-to-one function
D) Represents a linear function

ANSWER
B

6. Which statement is true about all functions?

A) Each input has exactly one output.
B) Each input has at least one output.
C) Each output has exactly one input.
D) Each output has at least one input.

ANSWER
A

Which of the following is NOT true about a function?
A) Each member of the domain is paired with exactly one member of the range
B) It can be represented by a set of ordered pairs
C) It can be represented by a set of connections by arrows
D) Each member of the domain is paired with more than one member of the range

ANSWER
D

8. How are functions represented through mapping?

A) By a set of vertical lines passing through the graph
B) By a set of connections by arrows
C) By a set of horizontal lines passing through the graph
D) By a set of points plotted on a graph

ANSWER
B

9. When is a graph of a mathematical relation considered a function?
A) If any vertical line drawn passing through the graph touches the graph at more than one point
B) If any vertical line drawn passing through the graph touches the graph at exactly one point
C) If any horizontal line drawn passing through the graph touches the graph at more than one point
D) If any horizontal line drawn passing through the graph touches the graph at exactly one point

ANSWER
B

10. What is a relation in mathematics?

A) A set of all the x-components of ordered pairs
B) A set of all the y-components of ordered pairs
C) Any set of ordered pairs
D) A set of all the z-components of ordered pairs

ANSWER
C

ANSWER
